The design keeps a single Blazor WebAssembly PWA UI surface, separates UI orchestration from application/domain logic, isolates IndexedDB persistence behind a small application service and infrastructure adapter, and records assumptions, exclusions, validation hooks, and rejected alternatives in the required managed artifact.","branchOutcomeKey":"","branchOutcomeTitle":"","evidenceRefs":["artifacts/process-runs/8476b73f-6ab3-4e0b-be97-dc501dbfc71e/steps/classify-dotnet-application.md","artifacts/process-runs/8476b73f-6ab3-4e0b-be97-dc501dbfc71e/steps/draft-architecture-design.md"],"nextActions":["Proceed to the scaffold/setup step using the grounded blazorwasm --pwa app contract, TetrisGame solution name, and xUnit test project contract.","During implementation, keep component event handlers thin and place game rules, scoring, and persistence behind application/domain boundaries.","Validate that the visible game route renders the play surface and that score persistence remains isolated behind the application service boundary."],"humanReadableSummaryMarkdown":"Status: Completed

Drafted the .NET architecture design for **TetrisGame** as a **Blazor WebAssembly PWA** with one runnable UI host and one xUnit test project. The artifact defines the UI/application/domain/infrastructure split, the game and score models, the orchestration and persistence services, the local-only IndexedDB boundary, test seams, validation hooks, and rejected alternatives.
